# Audit timeout constants: single source of truth shared across audit/test skills

## Problem statement

AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT (90s), AUDIT_HOST_LOCK_TIMEOUT (90s) and TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT (600s) are each independently defined and tuned in their owning skill, with only a comment tying AUDIT_HOST_LOCK_TIMEOUT to AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT. Tuning one budget silently diverges from its documented twin, so the two host and queue budgets drift apart and the intended invariant (host wait stays inside the parent bash-tool ~120s execution timeout, queue admission stays inside it too) is only enforced by comments.

## Users

- **Agent operators** — when they tune timeout values via environment variables, they expect related timeouts to remain consistent.
- **Contributors** — when they need to adjust a timeout, they want a single place to change it and know the implications.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 - Shared timeout module**: a single source of truth for audit/test wait budgets lives in a shared module (e.g. `skill/shared/wait_budgets.py` or an extension of `process_semaphore.py`), consumed by both `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` and `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`.
2. **AC2 - No behavioural change**: default values are unchanged (AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT=90, AUDIT_HOST_LOCK_TIMEOUT=90, TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT=600) and env-var overrides still win; existing tests pass unchanged.
3. **AC3 - Drift impossible**: the documented 'host timeout matches queue timeout / stays inside parent bash-tool timeout' invariant is enforced by the shared definition, not by a comment.
4. **AC4 - Docs**: audit-skill reference and test-skill reference point at the shared module for wait-budget tuning.

## Impact

Audit and test timeout values are defined in one shared module, eliminating the risk of silent drift when tuning individual budgets.

## Constraints

- Keep wait budgets configurable via env vars only (`AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT`, `AUDIT_HOST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR`); no config-file changes.
- Surgical change: audit/test concurrency semantics (priority queue, bounded wait, fail-fast on `AUDIT_LOCK_TIMEOUT=0`, cache-hit bypass) are unchanged.
- Full project test suite must pass.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/shared/wait_budgets.py` — New shared module exporting timeout defaults, env-var names, and helper functions.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Import and use shared constants instead of local definitions.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — Import and use shared constants instead of local definitions.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — Update references to point at shared module.
- `skill/test/SKILL.md` — Update references to point at shared module.
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — Update references.
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — Update references.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_concurrency.py` — Update imports to use shared constants.
- `skill/test/tests/test_test_skill_semaphore.py` — Update imports to use shared constants.

## Related work

- SA-0MTG5RYH8005RQNM (audit priority queue integration) — defined AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT
- SA-0MTG5U75A001F1RG (test skill shared concurrency primitive) — TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT
- SA-0MUSZJRB9006ZCHE (right-size audit concurrency ceilings) — AUDIT_HOST_LOCK_TIMEOUT default 90s
- SA-0MTG5U75A001F1RG (test skill shared concurrency primitive)
- SA-0MUSZJRB9006ZCHE (right-size audit concurrency ceilings)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Test imports**: existing tests import `*_DEFAULT` and `*_ENV` directly from their owning modules. After consolidation, tests must import from the shared module. Mitigation: update all test imports.
- **Scope creep**: the refactor could accidentally touch unrelated parts. Mitigation: surgical edits only, target only timeout constant definitions.
- **Env-var override consistency**: all callers must continue to honour the same env var names. Mitigation: shared module exports env-var names as constants alongside defaults.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No questions — the work item provides sufficient detail to proceed.

data.description:
## Goal

Emit structured, queryable contention telemetry from every semaphore wait in the
paced `test` / `test-fast` / `audit` / `audit-host` namespaces, so the ceilings and
timeouts (`TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY`, `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_FAST`, `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`,
`AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY`, `AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT`, `AUDIT_HOST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`) can be
tuned from counted wait distributions instead of guesswork.

## Problem statement

Today contention evidence only exists as (a) free-text log lines (`Audit slot
acquired: …`, `Implement run_tests: test slot acquired — queued_at=… wait_seconds=…`)
and (b) post-hoc scraping of pi session logs by `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py`.
Both miss the two facts tuning needs most: **how often** a wait happens at all, and
**how often the bounded wait expires** (`TestConcurrencyTimeout`, the audit
"concurrency limit reached" verdict). `Semaphore.acquire()` — the single choke point
every paced consumer passes through — records nothing. Without that record, the
deadlock/starvation class tracked by SA-0MTG0Y34T007ZHPF and SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86 can
regress invisibly, and every ceiling decision is an anecdote.

## Users

- **Agent operator tuning the host pools** — "When full suites start queuing again I
  want p90 wait and timeout counts per namespace, so I can decide between raising
  `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` and raising `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` without guessing."
- **Agent diagnosing a stalled gate** — "When my finish gate reports `slot_busy` I want
  to know whether the pool was saturated by three other suites or whether one waiter
  held a slot for an hour, so I know whether to wait or escalate."
- **Framework maintainer** — "After changing the semaphore I want the wait distribution
  before and after, so a fairness fix is proven rather than asserted."

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every `Semaphore.acquire()` wait in the paced namespaces (`test`, `test-fast`, `audit`,
  `audit-host`) appends one JSON-lines event to a configurable telemetry directory, with
  the fields `event`, `namespace`, `max_workers`, `timeout_seconds`, `queued_at`,
  `acquired_at`, `wait_seconds`, `outcome` (`acquired` | `timeout`), `deadline_expired`,
  `ticket`, `pid` and an optional `consumer` label; a fail-fast acquire (`timeout=0`) and
  a re-entrant no-op emit no wait event.
- Bounded-wait expiry is recorded with the same schema: `TestConcurrencyTimeout` from
  `run_tests.py` (both lanes) and the audit `AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT` /
  `AUDIT_HOST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` verdicts appear as `outcome=timeout,
  deadline_expired=true` events carrying the configured bound — with no new exception
  types and no change to concurrency semantics.
- `skill/shared/contention_summary.py` aggregates a telemetry directory into a
  deterministic human or JSON report — per-namespace event count, p50/p90/p99/max
  `wait_seconds`, timeout count and rate, and a wait-bucket (slot-saturation) histogram —
  and acquires no semaphore, touches no worklog and writes no file.
- Telemetry is off the acquire fast path and bounded: it is written once the wait
  resolves (never inside the poll loop), a single `O_APPEND` write that swallows and
  debug-logs its own errors, disabled by an env kill switch, size-rotated with a retained
  previous file, and isolated in tests so the host-wide pool and telemetry file are never
  touched (`PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` / telemetry-dir overrides).
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` and `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` document the
  event schema, the kill switch, the summary commands, and a worked "how to tune which env
  var from which number" procedure; the new behaviour is covered by unit tests (semaphore
  emission, expiry schema, aggregation over synthetic fixtures) and the full project test
  suite passes.

## Impact

Operators can see how long test and audit runs actually queue and how often they give up
waiting, instead of guessing which concurrency ceiling or timeout to change.

## Constraints

- **No latency on the acquire path.** Nothing may be written inside the retry loop;
  the event is emitted after the wait resolves (acquired or expired). One append per
  wait, no fsync, no floating-point formatting loops.
- **Fail-open, always.** A telemetry error (read-only dir, disk full, unparsable
  directory) is swallowed and logged at debug level — it must never change an acquire
  outcome, a run's exit status, or a cache entry.
- **No behavioural change to concurrency semantics.** Ceiling, bounded wait, jitter,
  turnstile fairness, nested-run isolation and cache-hit bypass all stay byte-identical.
  With telemetry disabled the acquire path must be indistinguishable from today.
- **No second session-log scraper.** `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` (SA-0MW7C69KU008ZT5K)
  already attributes waits from pi session logs and stays the historical backfill path.
  The new summary reads the JSONL stream as its primary source; it must not re-implement
  log scraping, and the two sources must never be summed together.
- **Respect the isolation contract:** telemetry honours `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` (and its own
  override), so a nested run's events never land in the host-wide pool's telemetry, and a
  test fixture spawning a nested runner is isolated automatically.
- **Bounded on disk:** append-only files grow forever otherwise; a size cap with one
  retained rotation (the `downtime-dispatches.log` precedent) keeps host hygiene.
- Framework repo boundaries: changes land in `skill/shared/`, `skill/test/`, `skill/audit/`
  and `docs/dev/`. UK English throughout.

## Existing state

- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — `Semaphore.acquire()` is the single choke point:
  it allocates a fairness ticket, polls the slot pool (~50 ms cadence, jittered), and
  raises `TimeoutError` at the deadline. It has no recording hook; `last_ticket` is the
  only diagnostic today.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `_test_concurrency_slot()` wraps the semaphore and
  converts `TimeoutError` into `TestConcurrencyTimeout`; `paced_runner(runner, on_wait=…)`
  already reports `(queued_at, wait_seconds)` to callers, and `run_suite` records the wait
  into each result's `slot_wait_seconds`. Two lanes exist (`test` ceiling 6,
  `test-fast` ceiling 4, both bounded by `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` = 600 s, `TEST_LOCK_JITTER`
  = 0.1).
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — two namespaces (`audit` admission with
  `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY`/`AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT`, and `audit-host` ingress with
  `AUDIT_MAX_HOST_AUDITS`/`AUDIT_HOST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`); waits are reported as stderr text
  (`Audit slot acquired: … wait_seconds=…`) and never persisted.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — finish-gate suites route through
  `paced_runner(on_wait=_log_test_slot_wait)`, emitting another stderr line
  (`Implement run_tests: test slot acquired — …`).
- `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` + `tests/test_measure_slot_wait.py` — read-only
  post-hoc attribution over pi session logs (three call-site categories, de-duplication,
  genuine-run filter). `skill/shared/audit_gate_metrics.py` similarly scrapes logs for
  audit queue admission. Both prove the *need* for the data and the absence of an
  emission point.
- Docs `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` §slot wait / §re-measuring and
  `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` §concurrency describe the tuning knobs but give no
  telemetry-driven procedure.

## Desired change

1. **Emission in `Semaphore`** — add an opt-out telemetry recorder used by
   `acquire()`: capture `queued_at` (wall clock) and a monotonic start, then, after the
   wait resolves, append one JSONL event per wait (acquired or expired). A `timeout=0`
   fail-fast acquire and a re-entrant no-op emit nothing (they are not waits). An optional
   constructor keyword (e.g. `consumer="implement-finish"`) labels the call site; the
   label defaults to the namespace so an unlabelled producer still aggregates usefully.
2. **Timeout events with the same schema** — the expiry path in `acquire()` emits
   `outcome=timeout, deadline_expired=true`; `_test_concurrency_slot()` and the audit
   admission/ingress call sites keep raising exactly what they raise today, so
   `TestConcurrencyTimeout` and the audit "concurrency limit reached" verdict continue to
   work and gain no new fields they must interpret.
3. **Aggregation helper** — `skill/shared/contention_summary.py` reads the telemetry
   directory (`--dir`, `--since`, `--namespace`, `--json`/`--human`) and reports counts,
   p50/p90/p99/max waits, timeout counts and rates, and a saturation histogram (e.g.
   `0–1 s`, `1–10 s`, `10–60 s`, `60–300 s`, `>300 s`). Malformed lines are counted and
   skipped, never fatal. Under-sampled namespaces are labelled rather than quoted.
4. **Tuning procedure** — docs gain a table mapping each env var to the number that
   justifies changing it (e.g. high p90 with zero expiries ⇒ raise the ceiling; a
   non-trivial expiry rate with idle capacity ⇒ the bound is too short; `>300 s` waits
   with free slots ⇒ a fairness/starvation defect, not a ceiling problem).
5. **Tests** — semaphore emission (acquired, expired, fail-fast silent, re-entrant
   silent, kill switch off, telemetry failure fail-open), aggregation over synthetic
   JSONL fixtures (percentiles, histogram, timeout rate, malformed lines, empty dir), and
   an isolation test proving a nested-run directory keeps its events out of the host pool.

Documented assumptions (to confirm or correct in review):

- **Default telemetry location** — a `contention/` subdirectory of the semaphore base dir
  (`<PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR or XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/pi-semaphores>/contention`), overridable with an
  explicit env var so the host can point it at persistent storage. Reusing the semaphore
  base gives tests and nested runs isolation for free; the trade-off is that the runtime-dir
  default does not survive a reboot, which the docs call out and the override fixes.
- **Kill switch name/shape** — an opt-out boolean env var (e.g. `PI_CONTENTION_TELEMETRY=0`)
  rather than opt-in, because AC1 requires every wait to be recorded by default.
- **One event per wait, not per poll** — a poll-cadence event stream would be orders of
  magnitude larger and would itself perturb the herd behaviour it measures.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Telemetry perturbs what it measures.** A write per *poll* would multiply the I/O of a
  saturated herd; the design records one event per *wait*, after it resolves. Residual
  risk: a host with hundreds of short waits gains hundreds of appends — mitigated by the
  single-`O_APPEND` write, the size cap, and the kill switch.
- **Disk growth / lost history.** An unbounded append file fills a runtime tmpfs; a
  rotation cap with one retained file bounds it. Conversely the default location may not
  survive a reboot, so a host that wants multi-day tuning data must set the override —
  documented, not silently assumed.
- **Test-suite cost and pollution.** Default-on emission means every isolate-and-acquire
  test in the suite writes a file. Mitigation: the telemetry dir follows the semaphore
  base dir (already a `tmp_path` in existing fixtures), the suite asserts a nested run
  stays isolated, and a test proves the kill switch and fail-open paths add no failure
  mode to the acquire path.
- **Double counting with the existing measurement.** Wait data now exists in three places
  (JSONL events, stderr lines, session logs). The constraint is explicit: the JSONL stream
  is the primary source, stderr lines stay for human log continuity, and
  `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` remains the historical backfill — never summed.
- **Scope creep.** Adjacent opportunities surfaced during context gathering — automatic
  nested-run isolation (SA-0MVEDN5IS001OYQF), a second aggregation front-end for the audit
  queue, retention dashboards — are *not* in scope; they stay linked work items.
- **Assumption:** the semaphore is genuinely the single choke point. If a consumer acquires
  a slot by another mechanism (a bespoke `flock` outside `Semaphore`), its waits will be
  invisible; the emission point is chosen because all four paced namespaces route through
  `Semaphore.acquire()`, and the aggregation's per-namespace counts would expose a gap.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — actual emission point: `acquire()` capture/emit,
  recorder helper, telemetry-dir resolution, kill switch, error swallowing; re-export the
  recorder for callers.
- `skill/shared/contention_summary.py` — new read-only aggregation CLI (JSON by default,
  `--human` summary), replacing nothing and acquiring nothing.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_process_semaphore.py` — existing suite; add emission,
  fail-fast-silent, kill-switch, fail-open and isolation coverage with a tmp telemetry dir.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_contention_summary.py` — new fixture-driven aggregation tests.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `_test_concurrency_slot()` / `paced_runner()` pass a
  `consumer` label per lane and prove `TestConcurrencyTimeout` still surfaces unchanged.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — label the `audit` admission and `audit-host`
  ingress acquisitions; keep verdict text unchanged.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — label the finish-gate paced runner (its
  `on_wait` line stays for log continuity).
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — event schema, kill switch, summary commands, tuning
  table; cross-reference (not re-scrape) `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py`.
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — the same for `AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT` /
  `AUDIT_HOST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` / `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY`.

## Related work

- SA-0MTG5U75A001F1RG — test-skill shared concurrency primitive (defines the ceiling,
  the bounded wait and `TestConcurrencyTimeout`).
- SA-0MTG0Y34T007ZHPF — multi-agent audit/test coordination: the deadlock class this
  telemetry makes observable.
- SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86 — nested-run semaphore isolation: the `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` contract
  telemetry must honour (and, still open as SA-0MVEDN5IS001OYQF, the item that would make
  isolation automatic).
- SA-0MUA8BSAG000YZA2 — pacing telemetry: the `on_wait` hook and its `slot_wait_seconds`
  reporting; this item supplies the persisted stream beneath it.
- SA-0MVEDOF7A004TSWD — staggered back-off/jitter: a fairness change whose before/after
  distributions this telemetry should make measurable.
- Arrival-ordered turnstile (cited as SA-0MVSJX5HS002DJHI in the
  `process_semaphore.py` docstring; that id lives outside this worklog store) — slot
  fairness/starvation, whose queue-position waits are the `>300 s` bucket the summary
  reports.
- SA-0MVWZQ269009SJXV — full/fast lane split (why `test-fast` must be in scope, not just
  `test`).
- SA-0MVWKZ4QD006L2E0 — dynamic slot discovery (a ceiling symptom this telemetry would
  have caught earlier).
- SA-0MW7C69KU008ZT5K — `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py`, the existing read-only
  session-log measurement this item must not duplicate.
- SA-0MVTET8KQ0031R6Z — finish-gate classification that reports slot wait separately; the
  consumer of the same measurement.
- SA-0MTG5RYH8005RQNM / SA-0MUSZJRB9006ZCHE — audit bounded priority queue and its tuning
  (the audit-side numbers this telemetry would supply directly).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No operator questions were required: every open point was resolved by inspecting the
repository, and each remaining decision is recorded above as a **documented assumption**
with its trade-off so a producer can correct it in review.

- **Q1 (agent, resolved by inspection):** Does an emission point already exist, or does
  telemetry already persist anywhere? **Answer:** No. `Semaphore.acquire()` records
  nothing; `paced_runner(on_wait=…)` only hands `(queued_at, wait_seconds)` to the caller,
  which logs a stderr line and folds the value into each result's `slot_wait_seconds`.
  Evidence: `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py::Semaphore.acquire`,
  `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py::paced_runner`, `…::run_suite`.
- **Q2 (agent, resolved by inspection):** Is this a duplicate of the existing measurement
  harness? **Answer:** No. `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` is a *post-hoc* parser over pi
  session logs (SA-0MW7C69KU008ZT5K) with a genuine-run filter; it cannot see waits that
  produced no log line and cannot see expiry at all. This item adds the *emission* side and
  a summary over that stream; the constraint "no second session-log scraper" keeps the two
  from diverging. Evidence: `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py`, `tests/test_measure_slot_wait.py`,
  `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` §"Re-measuring post-fix slot wait".
- **Q3 (agent, resolved by inspection):** Which namespaces must be covered? The seed AC1
  names `test` and `audit`. **Answer:** Four exist and all four are tuning knobs:
  `test` (`TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY`), `test-fast` (`TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_FAST`, split in
  SA-0MVWZQ269009SJXV — the lane partial runs actually wait in), `audit`
  (`AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY`/`AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT`) and `audit-host`
  (`AUDIT_MAX_HOST_AUDITS`/`AUDIT_HOST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`). Recording at the `Semaphore` level
  covers all four for free; the ACs name them explicitly so no lane is silently skipped.
  Evidence: `run_tests.py` constants and `_lane_semaphore_config`, `audit_runner.py`
  `AUDIT_SEMAPHORE_NAME` / `AUDIT_HOST_SEMAPHORE_NAME`.
- **Q4 (agent, resolved by inspection):** Where should the telemetry file live?
  **Answer:** Under the semaphore base directory by default, because that is the directory
  tests and nested runs already isolate via `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR`
  (`skill/shared/process_semaphore.py::nested_semaphore_dir`, docs §"Nested-run isolation");
  an explicit override lets a host keep it on persistent storage. The persistence
  trade-off is recorded as an assumption, not silently chosen.

data.description:
# Automatic nested-run semaphore isolation — inherited marker instead of an opt-in convention

## Problem statement

A top-level `run_tests.py` execution holds a host-wide `"test"` semaphore slot for its whole
duration, so any *nested* invocation of the runner (in-process or as a subprocess) that
resolves the same pool queues behind the slot its own outer run is holding — and can wait out
the full `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` (measured: 2700 s hangs in `implement.py finish` and the pre-push
gate). Since SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86 the fix is an **opt-in convention**: each fixture must remember
to point `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` at an isolated directory. Nothing in the runner enforces it, so a
future test, harness or project that forgets re-introduces the deadlock silently. The live-repo
guard already solved the analogous recursion problem with an inherited marker
(`LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE`) that nested runs detect and stand down on; the test semaphore needs
the same treatment, so isolation becomes the default rather than a memory exercise.

## Users

- **Test author adding a subprocess-spawning test** — "I add a test that shells out to
  `run_tests.py`; I want it to work without knowing that a semaphore convention exists."
- **Framework maintainer / operator** — "I want the isolation guarantee to live in the runner
  (one place, next to the acquire), not in every project's `conftest.py`, node suite or shell
  harness."
- **Agent running a gate under concurrent load** — "I want the finish gate or pre-push hook to
  never deadlock because a test nested a runner inside a held slot."
- **Operator who deliberately shapes namespaces** — "I want an explicit `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` to
  keep winning, so I can still place a run's pool where I choose."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Automatic isolation marker**: a run that holds a host-wide `"test"` (or `"test-fast"`)
   slot exports an inherited marker to its environment for the duration of the hold — e.g.
   `TEST_SEMAPHORE_SLOT_HELD=<resolved semaphore base dir>`. The marker is set and cleared by the
   same code that acquires and releases the slot (`run_tests.py::_test_concurrency_slot`), so it
   cannot drift from the real acquisition; the value identifies the pool actually held, and a
   nested hold restores the outer value instead of clearing it.
2. **AC2 — Nested runs auto-isolate**: when the runner starts and the marker is already present
   while `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` is not, it derives an isolated namespace automatically (a
   per-invocation directory beneath the marker's base dir, e.g.
   `<marker-base>/nested/<pid>-<nonce>`) and bounds itself there instead of contending for the
   inherited pool — no fixture opt-in and no code at the call site.
3. **AC3 — Explicit override still wins**: an explicitly-set `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` takes precedence
   over the automatic derivation, so existing fixtures and operators keep full control of the
   namespace.
4. **AC4 — Host-wide ceiling preserved**: top-level runs (marker absent) still bound themselves
   via `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` / `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_FAST`, unchanged; only nested invocations
   isolate. Cache-hit runs acquire no slot and therefore set no marker.
5. **AC5 — Regression test**: a test holds an outer slot in a known pool and spawns a nested
   `run_tests.py` **without** setting `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` in the child environment (the marker is
   inherited), and asserts the nested run reports success and finishes well inside the outer
   hold — the test's own subprocess timeout (e.g. 30 s) is the measurable bound, versus the
   `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` it would otherwise serve. A companion assertion proves an explicit
   `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` in the child still wins over the derived directory.
6. **AC6 — Docs**: `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` (§0.6 nested-run isolation) and
   `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` document the inherited marker as the **default** contract, with
   the `nested_semaphore_dir()` fixture helper retained as the explicit-control path; the
   `run_tests.py` and `process_semaphore.py` module docstrings and the repo-root `conftest.py`
   fixture docstring are updated to describe the new default.
7. **AC7 — All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Impact

Any test, harness or project that nests a `run_tests.py` invocation while an outer run holds a
slot now isolates itself automatically, so the 600-second nested-run deadlock cannot come back
just because a future test author did not know about a `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` convention.

## Constraints

- **Inheritance through the normal environment chain only.** The marker is set on the process's
  own environment for the duration of the hold and removed (or restored) on release — mirroring
  `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` in `guarded_run_all`, which sets the marker only when it is absent and
  pops it only when it set it. **Fidelity note:** the seed's "no global mutation of the parent's
  own environment" is read as *no permanent or unscoped* mutation — the guard pattern it names
  does temporarily set and then restore `os.environ`, and this item follows exactly that shape.
  No scrubbing of unrelated variables and no second isolation mechanism.
- **No weakening of host-wide bounding.** A genuine top-level parallel suite still contends for
  the configured ceiling; isolation applies only to invocations that are demonstrably nested.
- **Backwards compatible.** Existing fixtures that set `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` explicitly keep working
  unchanged (explicit wins), including the repo-root autouse fixture in `conftest.py`.
- **No behavioural change to slot fairness, ceilings, jitter or cache semantics** — the marker
  and derivation are additive; cache keys and command strings are byte-identical.
- **Framework repo boundaries:** changes land in `skill/test/`, `skill/shared/` and `docs/dev/`.
  UK English throughout; CHANGELOG is managed by the ship pipeline.

## Existing state

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py::_test_concurrency_slot` (line ~2623) is the single place a
  test-run slot is acquired, for both lanes (`_lane_semaphore_config`: `test` /
  `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` default 6; `test-fast` / `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_FAST` default 4, bounded
  by `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` default 600 s with `TEST_LOCK_JITTER` default 0.1). It constructs
  `Semaphore(semaphore_name, …)` with **no directory argument**; the namespace comes from
  `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` resolved inside `Semaphore.__init__` via `_default_lock_dir()`
  (`skill/shared/process_semaphore.py`, lines ~176-200, ~291-311).
- Slot acquisition sites: `_cached_runner` (~2812), the paced `_paced` runner (~2881) and the
  lane fallback path (~3580). Cache-served results never acquire a slot.
- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py::nested_semaphore_dir(base_dir)` (line ~206) returns
  `<base_dir>/pi-semaphores`; it is the opt-in helper fixtures call today.
- `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` is the proven recursion-marker pattern:
  `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py::MARKER_ENV` and
  `run_tests.py::guarded_run_all` (~4286-4312) set it only when absent and clear it only when
  they set it, so nested guards stand down and an outer guard is never disarmed. The test
  semaphore has no equivalent.
- The opt-in convention is spread across call sites: `tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py`
  (autouse fixture + `_child_env`), `tests/test_pytest_path_resolution.py`,
  `tests/test_run_tests_cache.py`, `tests/test_pre_push_gate_*`,
  `skill/test/tests/test_guarded_run_all.py`, `tests/test_validate_test_fanout.py` and the
  repo-root `conftest.py::_isolated_test_semaphore_dir` autouse fixture (which gives each
  **pytest** test its own `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR`).
- Existing regression coverage: `skill/test/tests/test_nested_semaphore_isolation.py` (AC1
  isolated nested run completes, AC3 non-isolated nested run waits bounded, two concurrent
  outers) and `skill/shared/tests/test_process_semaphore.py::test_nested_namespace_never_queues_in_the_host_turnstile`.
- Docs: `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` §0.6 and `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` describe
  isolation as a fixture obligation.

## Desired change

1. **Marker constant and set/clear in `_test_concurrency_slot`.** Add an env constant (e.g.
   `TEST_SEMAPHORE_MARKER_ENV = "TEST_SEMAPHORE_SLOT_HELD"`). On entry, resolve the base
   directory of the pool about to be acquired (`<base>/<namespace>` parent — the value must name
   the pool actually held, not the derived child), save any existing marker, publish it, and on
   exit restore the saved value (or remove the marker when this call published it). Cache-hit
   paths are untouched — they hold no slot.
2. **Detection and derivation at nest time.** In `_test_concurrency_slot`, when the marker is
   already present *and* `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` is unset, derive a per-invocation isolated namespace
   beneath the marker's base directory and bound the acquisition there. Precedence, highest
   first: explicit `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` → automatic derivation (marker present) → ambient default
   pool (top-level). The derived directory must be unique per invocation (pid + short nonce) so
   two nested runs never share a pool by accident.
3. **Namespace plumbing without temp env mutation.** Preferred: give `Semaphore.__init__` an
   optional `base_dir: str | Path | None = None` parameter (default `None` keeps
   `_default_lock_dir()`), so the derived directory is passed explicitly and `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR`
   is never temporarily rewritten underneath other code. Fallback if a constructor parameter is
   rejected at plan time: save/set/restore `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` around the nested acquisition and
   document the single-threaded-runner assumption. Either way the marker remains the only
   inherited contract.
4. **Fixture helper retained.** `nested_semaphore_dir()` stays as the explicit-control helper for
   fixtures that want a known directory; the repo-root `conftest.py` autouse fixture stays as
   belt-and-braces (its docstring gains a pointer to the new default so the two layers do not
   drift).
5. **Tests** (new cases in `skill/test/tests/test_nested_semaphore_isolation.py`, plus a helper
   unit test in `skill/shared/tests/test_process_semaphore.py` when the `base_dir` parameter
   lands): marker published while a slot is held and cleared on release; nested run with marker
   set and `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` unset completes within a few seconds while the outer pool is
   saturated; explicit `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` in the child still wins; top-level run (marker absent)
   still queues on the host pool; two nested runs derive distinct directories; lane coverage for
   `test-fast` (or a documented reason it is one shared code path).
6. **Docs** — see AC6/AC7: the marker name, its value, the precedence order, the derived
   directory shape and the remaining explicit-override escape hatch.

Documented assumptions (to confirm or correct in review):

- **A1 — The live risk is narrower than the seed implies, and the change is still worth it.**
  The repo-root `conftest.py` autouse fixture already isolates every *pytest* test in this
  repository by pointing `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` at a per-test directory, so the current in-repo
  blast radius is limited to (a) fixtures that build a child environment explicitly and drop
  `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR`, (b) non-pytest suites (`node:test`, vitest, shell harnesses) and other
  repositories with no such safety net, and (c) in-process double nesting where the outer hold
  and the nested acquire share one explicit directory. The automatic marker is still the right
  fix: it moves the guarantee from a per-repository fixture convention to the acquisition point
  itself.
- **A2 — Marker value carries the held base directory**, not a bare `"1"`. A boolean marker
  cannot name a derivation parent, and the seed's AC2 explicitly allows a per-invocation
  directory "under the marker's parent". The value therefore doubles as the derivation root and
  as a diagnostic in logs.
- **A3 — Derivation happens per invocation, never per run-scoped root.** AC2 permits "a
  run-scoped root", but a unique per-invocation directory cannot be shared by two concurrent
  nested runs and needs no locking or cleanup beyond the runtime dir's existing lifecycle.
- **A4 — `test-fast` shares the code path.** Both lanes go through `_test_concurrency_slot`, so
  one implementation covers them; the docs name both ceilings and the tests cover at least one
  fast-lane case.
- **A5 — External-item overlap is co-ordinated, not resolved here.** SA-0MVB713IZ000NO42
  (migrate `test_nested_semaphore_isolation.py`'s `_make_noop_project` to `git_sandbox`) touches
  the same test file from a different branch of work; whichever lands second rebases. No
  dependency edge is created at intake.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — new marker constant, set/restore in
  `_test_concurrency_slot`, nested detection + derivation, module docstring (§nested-run
  isolation) updated.
- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — optional `base_dir=` on `Semaphore.__init__` (AC2
  plumbing), a helper for a unique per-invocation nested directory, docstring update next to
  `nested_semaphore_dir`.
- `skill/test/tests/test_nested_semaphore_isolation.py` — AC5 regression tests (marker set /
  cleared, auto-isolation without `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR`, explicit override wins).
- `skill/shared/tests/test_process_semaphore.py` — `base_dir=` unit coverage alongside the
  existing nested-namespace test (if the constructor change lands).
- `conftest.py` — docstring cross-reference only (no behaviour change).
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — §0.6 rewritten around the marker as the default contract.
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` — semaphore-isolation subsection documenting the marker and the
  remaining explicit-override path.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Marker leaks into unrelated children.** While a slot is held, every subprocess the suite
  spawns inherits the marker; only `run_tests.py` consumers act on it, and the derived directory
  is per invocation, so the effect is confined to runners that were already nested. Mitigation:
  the explicit-`PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` precedence path remains and the docs state the contract.
- **Process-wide env mutation under threads.** `os.environ` is process-wide; if future work runs
  suites in threads, two holds could interleave save/restore. Mitigation: set only when absent
  and clear only when this call set it (the `guarded_run_all` pattern), and prefer the
  `base_dir=` constructor parameter so the derivation never depends on env mutation. Today the
  runner executes suites sequentially, so the risk is latent; it is recorded rather than solved.
- **Derived directories accumulate.** Per-invocation dirs hold slot files after release, like
  every semaphore directory today, under the runtime dir; they are empty of processes and
  cleared on reboot. Mitigation: name them under one `<base>/nested/` parent so a future prune
  can target them, and document the location.
- **Regression-test cost and flake surface.** AC5 spawns real `run_tests.py` subprocesses. Mitigation:
  reuse the existing no-op project fixture (`_make_noop_project`) and short explicit subprocess
  timeouts, as `test_nested_semaphore_isolation.py` already does, so the proof is fast and cannot
  itself hang the suite.
- **The conftest safety net could mask a broken derivation.** With `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` already
  set per test, the automatic path is rarely exercised in-repo. Mitigation: AC5's regression test
  constructs the child environment explicitly (marker present, `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` absent) instead
  of relying on ambient conftest state.
- **Silent isolation hides genuine contention.** A nested run that auto-isolates no longer
  queues, so a future *top-level* contention problem could be misread as a nested one. Mitigation:
  the marker value and derived path are visible in the run's environment/log context, and
  SA-0MVEDMM3N004Y6MO's contention telemetry records waits per namespace.
- **Scope creep.** Adjacent opportunities — removing the repo-root conftest fixture, giving
  audit semaphores the same marker, and telemetry for derived namespaces — are *not* in scope;
  they stay linked work items.
- **Assumption:** the marker plus one derivation point covers every nesting shape
  (subprocess → subprocess, in-process → subprocess, in-process → in-process). Each deeper level
  sees the marker its immediate parent published, and AC1's restore-on-release keeps the chain
  honest; the AC5 test covers the primary subprocess shape and the derivation is unit-tested.

## Related work

- **SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86** — introduced `nested_semaphore_dir()` + opt-in `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR`
  isolation (completed); this item makes isolation the default and the helper the explicit path.
- **SA-0MUG30J5F001L57H / SA-0MUH1MJL6003767Q** — `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` recursion marker, the
  pattern to mirror (set-if-absent, clear-only-if-set).
- **SA-0MVEDMM3N004Y6MO** — test/audit semaphore contention telemetry (in progress); records
  waits per namespace, which is how an auto-isolated nested run stays observable.
- **SA-0MVB713IZ000NO42** — migrate `test_nested_semaphore_isolation.py` helpers to
  `git_sandbox` (blocked, different scope, same file — rebase co-ordination only).
- **SA-0MUA8BSAG000YZA2** — pacing via the shared semaphore (`TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY`), whose
  host-wide bounding AC4 must preserve.
- **SA-0MVSJX5HS002DJHI** — arrival-ordered turnstile; isolation must keep the nested namespace's
  turnstile separate from the host one (already true, re-asserted by AC2).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No operator questions were required: every open point was resolved by inspecting the repository,
and each remaining decision is recorded above as a **documented assumption** with its trade-off so
a producer can correct it in review.

- **Q1 (agent, resolved by inspection):** Is there already any automatic detection of nested
  runner invocations? **Answer:** No. `_test_concurrency_slot` constructs a `Semaphore` with no
  directory argument and no marker; isolation exists only as the `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` fixture
  convention from SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86. Evidence: `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py::_test_concurrency_slot`,
  `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py::_default_lock_dir`, `::nested_semaphore_dir`.
- **Q2 (agent, resolved by inspection):** Does the repo already isolate nested runs well enough
  that this item is redundant? **Answer:** Partially — the repo-root `conftest.py` autouse
  fixture `_isolated_test_semaphore_dir` gives every pytest test its own `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR`, so
  in-repo pytest nesting is already safe today. The convention is still opt-in per repository and
  per suite type (`node:test`/vitest/shell harnesses and other projects get nothing), and an
  explicitly constructed child environment can drop the variable. That narrows the problem
  statement (recorded as assumption A1) without removing the value of enforcing isolation at the
  acquisition point. Evidence: `conftest.py::_isolated_test_semaphore_dir`,
  `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` §0.6.
- **Q3 (agent, resolved by inspection):** Which pattern should the marker follow? **Answer:**
  `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` in `run_tests.py::guarded_run_all` — set only when absent, cleared
  only when this call set it, so an outer holder is never disarmed. Evidence:
  `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py::MARKER_ENV`, `run_tests.py` lines ~4286-4312.
- **Q4 (agent, resolved by inspection):** Can the derived namespace be passed without mutating
  `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR`? **Answer:** Yes — `Semaphore.__init__` currently resolves the base directory
  itself, so an optional `base_dir=` parameter (default `None` → `_default_lock_dir()`) lets the
  runner pass the derived directory explicitly. The alternative (temporary env rewrite) is
  recorded in the desired change with its thread-safety caveat. Evidence:
  `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` lines ~291-311.
- **Q5 (agent, resolved by inspection):** Does any other consumer need the marker? **Answer:** Not
  in scope. The audit semaphores (`audit`, `audit-host`) have their own namespaces and their own
  recursion concerns; the marker is namespaced to the test lanes and the docs state that. Evidence:
  `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` semaphore names.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MVB713IZ000NO42** – Migrate nested-semaphore fixture and validate_fanout (blocked)
- **SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86** – Test infra: concurrent full-suite runs deadlock on the host-wide test semaphore (completed)
- **SA-0MR3P8N3V001Q3RG** – Add rebuild step to implement SKILL.md after git pull (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: 0muh1mjl6003767q, 0muy6u05f008rg86, absent, ac1, ac2 (+152 more)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: absent, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+148 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: 0muh1mjl6003767q, absent, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+146 more)

---

## Plan (plan skill session, 2026-11-14)

**Scope decision — one vertical slice, no child work items.** The change is a
single atomic behaviour swap (isolation moves from a fixture convention to the
slot-acquisition point) across two modules and their docs: splitting it would
need a strict-`xfail` interim commit (the `SA-0MW0LONU30002G20` tests-only
pattern) for ~6 h of work, adding a second worktree/session cycle without
changing the outcome. Precedent in this family is the leaf item:
`SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86`, `SA-0MVEDOF7A004TSWD`, `SA-0MVWZQ269009SJXV`,
`SA-0MVXEQDI6005MK59` all shipped un-parented at comparable size. **Test-first
ordering is preserved inside the slice**: steps 1–2 are the failing tests.

### Implementation order

**Step 1 — Regression and unit tests first (must fail for the right reason).**

`skill/test/tests/test_nested_semaphore_isolation.py` (reuses
`_make_noop_project`; `_run_nested` gains an `unset=[...]` parameter so a child
environment can drop a variable explicitly instead of relying on ambient
state):

1. `test_slot_hold_publishes_and_restores_marker` — inside
   `_test_concurrency_slot()` the marker is present and equals the base
   directory of the pool actually held; after the block it is absent again
   (and the marker is absent when it was absent before).
2. `test_nested_hold_restores_outer_marker` — outer hold publishes; an
   in-process inner `_test_concurrency_slot()` republishes its own pool and, on
   exit, restores the outer value (never clears it) (AC1).
3. `test_nested_run_without_semaphore_dir_auto_isolates` — **AC5a, the money
   test**: outer in-process hold with `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR=<host>`,
   `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY=1`; the child `run_tests.py` is spawned with
   `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` **removed** (only the inherited marker), `--no-cache`,
   `subprocess(timeout=30)`. Asserts returncode 0 and `success: true`; the 30 s
   subprocess timeout is the measurable bound versus the `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`
   (600 s) it would otherwise serve (AC2, AC5).
4. `test_explicit_semaphore_dir_still_wins` — **AC5b/AC3**: same saturated
   outer hold, but the child sets `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR=<host>` explicitly *and*
   inherits the marker; `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT=1` makes it fail with the
   `concurrency slot` notice, proving the explicit namespace beat the
   derivation (a passing run here would mean the derivation overrode the
   operator).
5. `test_two_nested_runs_derive_distinct_directories` — two children with only
   the marker set complete concurrently and leave two distinct entries under
   `<host>/nested/` (AC2 uniqueness, documented assumption A3).
6. `test_fast_lane_hold_publishes_marker` — the marker contract holds for the
   `test-fast` lane via `_slot_lane("fast")` (AC1 lane coverage, A4).
7. `test_cached_run_sets_no_marker` — a cache-served `run_all` leaves the
   marker absent (AC4: cache hits acquire no slot).
8. `test_top_level_run_still_queues_without_marker` — **AC4**: the outer hold
   uses the *ambient* pool (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=<tmp>/runtime`, no
   `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR`), and the child env has the marker **removed** plus
   `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT=1`; it must fail with the `concurrency slot` notice,
   proving a marker-less (top-level) invocation still contends for the
   host-wide pool instead of deriving an isolated one.

`skill/shared/tests/test_process_semaphore.py`:

9. `test_base_dir_parameter_overrides_env_namespace` — `Semaphore(..., base_dir=tmp)`
   puts slot files under `<tmp>/<name>` even with `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` set to
   something else (AC3 plumbing).
10. `test_base_dir_defaults_to_resolved_lock_dir` — `base_dir=None` keeps
    today's `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` / runtime-dir resolution, and `sem.base_dir`
    reports the resolved base in **both** cases (single source for the marker
    value, decision D3).
11. `test_unique_nested_dir_is_per_invocation` — `unique_nested_dir(base)`
    returns `<base>/nested/<pid>-<nonce>`, two calls differ, and nothing is
    created eagerly.

Expected pre-implementation failure: missing `TEST_SEMAPHORE_SLOT_HELD`
constant, `TypeError` on `base_dir=`, no `unique_nested_dir`, no derivation.

**Step 2 — `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` (the plumbing).**

- Optional `base_dir: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None` on
  `Semaphore.__init__`; `self.base_dir = Path(base_dir) if base_dir is not None
  else _default_lock_dir()`; `self._slot_dir = self.base_dir /
  _sanitize_name(name)`. This is the item's **preferred** plumbing — the
  derived directory is passed explicitly, so `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` is never
  temporarily rewritten underneath other code (the temp-rewrite fallback is not
  needed; see decision D3).
- `NESTED_SUBDIR = "nested"` plus
  `unique_nested_dir(base_dir) -> Path` returning
  `<base>/nested/<pid>-<token_hex(4)>`; directory creation stays lazy inside
  `Semaphore`.
- `nested_semaphore_dir()` is **unchanged** (explicit-control helper, returns
  `<base>/pi-semaphores`) and its docstring gains a pointer to the new default
  contract; module docstring updated.

**Step 3 — `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` (marker + derivation).**

- `TEST_SEMAPHORE_MARKER_ENV = "TEST_SEMAPHORE_SLOT_HELD"` beside the other
  env constants (with a comment naming the `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` precedent).
- In `_test_concurrency_slot`, resolve the acquisition namespace with the AC's
  precedence, highest first: **explicit `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR`** →
  `base_dir=None` (env wins, byte-identical behaviour) → **marker present and
  `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` unset** → `base_dir=unique_nested_dir(marker)` → **neither**
  → `base_dir=None` (ambient top-level pool, unchanged ceiling).
- Marker lifecycle around the hold: capture `previous = os.environ.get(...)`,
  publish `sem.base_dir`, and in a `finally` restore `previous` when there was
  one, else `pop` it. Same save/restore shape as `guarded_run_all`, extended to
  republish the pool **actually held** (AC1; decision D1).
- Both lanes share this one code path (`_cached_runner`, the `paced_runner`
  body and the fast-lane rerun all call it); cache-hit paths never enter it, so
  they acquire no slot and set no marker.
- Module docstring + `_test_concurrency_slot` docstring rewritten: the
  inherited marker is the default contract, `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` the explicit
  escape hatch.

**Step 4 — fixture docstring cross-reference (no behaviour change).**
`conftest.py::_isolated_test_semaphore_dir` keeps its behaviour and gains a
one-line pointer to the marker default, so the two layers cannot drift
(retained as belt-and-braces, not the contract).

**Step 5 — docs.**
`docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` §0.6 rewritten around the marker (name,
value = held pool's base directory, precedence order, derived shape
`<base>/nested/<pid>-<nonce>`, restore-on-release, both lanes, the explicit
override, the `nested_semaphore_dir()` helper as the *explicit-control* path);
§0.5 env table gains the marker row. `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` gains a
nested-run semaphore isolation subsection alongside the other isolation
contracts (§9.x), cross-linked from §0.6, with the derived-directory location
and the "empty files, cleared on reboot, prune `<base>/nested/`" note.
`docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` nested-run sentence reworded to name
the marker as the default (finish-gate readers currently read it as a fixture
obligation). AC7 sweep verified during planning: the only in-repo references to
the convention are the files above plus `conftest.py`;
`README.md`/`docs/*.md` (outside `docs/dev`) say nothing about
`PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR`, and no LLM-wiki page covers it (`wiki_search` for the term
returns nothing), so no site entry needs updating — the implement session
re-runs that grep to confirm nothing new appeared.

**Step 6 — verification.**
Changed-scope runs through `/skill:test` at each step; the final
`implement.py finish` gate plus the dev-push full suite satisfy AC8. Heaviest
cost is step 1's subprocess tests — keep the 30 s child timeouts and
`--no-cache` so the proof cannot itself hang.

### Decisions recorded (producer may correct in review)

- **D1 — marker publish semantics: publish the pool actually held, restore the
  previous value on exit** (not the guard's strict set-if-absent). AC1 requires
  the value to name the pool actually held *and* requires a nested hold to
  restore the outer value rather than clear it; the save/set/restore shape is
  still the guard's — temporary, scoped, restored in `finally` — so the
  constraint's "mirroring `guarded_run_all`" and its "no permanent or unscoped
  mutation" reading both hold. The set-if-absent variant remains a one-line
  alternative if review prefers it.
- **D2 — marker lives on the process environment for the duration of the hold**
  (inheritance through the normal env chain only). The runner executes suites
  sequentially, so the save/restore is not thread-safe today; recorded in the
  code comment rather than solved (matches the item's risk register).
- **D3 — no temporary `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` rewrite**: the derivation is passed as
  `base_dir=` and `Semaphore.base_dir` is the single source of the marker
  value, so the published value cannot drift from the pool acquired.
- **D4 — `test-fast` shares the code path** (A4): one implementation, one
  fast-lane test, docs name both ceilings.
- **D5 — single slice, no children** (see *Scope decision* above).

### Out of scope (deliberately unchanged)

- Audit semaphores (`audit`, `audit-host`) get no marker — they own their
  recursion concerns; telemetry/tuning continues in `SA-0MVEDMM3N004Y6MO`.
- The repo-root `conftest.py` autouse fixture is **not** removed (belt and
  braces; it is no longer the contract).
- No changes to cache keys, command strings, ceilings, jitter, bounded waits,
  slot fairness or the turnstile namespace (`SA-0MVSJX5HS002DJHI` re-assert).
- No prune/cleanup automation for `<base>/nested/` (documented location only).

### Risks carried into implementation

- AC5 spawns real `run_tests.py` subprocesses: bounded by a 30 s child timeout,
  `_make_noop_project` (a `bash noop.sh` suite) and `--no-cache`, so the proof
  is fast and cannot hang the suite.
- The repo-root conftest fixture masks the automatic path in-repo; test 3
  builds the child environment explicitly (marker present,
  `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` removed) instead of relying on ambient state.
- Rebase co-ordination only with `SA-0MVB713IZ000NO42`, which edits the same
  test file (`_make_noop_project` → `git_sandbox`): whichever lands second
  rebases. No dependency edge.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers (plan session, 2026-11-14)

No operator questions were needed: every open point was answerable by
inspection, and the intake's clarifying-question appendix already resolved the
rest. The intake's documented assumptions (A1–A5) are accepted unchanged; the
plan adds D1–D5 above.

- **Q1 (agent, resolved by inspection):** Does `Semaphore.__init__` already
  accept a base directory, so the derived namespace can be passed without
  env mutation? **Answer:** No — it resolves `_default_lock_dir()` internally
  (`ENV_LOCK_DIR`/`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`/`tempfile.gettempdir()`), so the optional
  `base_dir=` parameter is the plumbing step. Evidence:
  `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` (`_default_lock_dir`, `Semaphore.__init__`
  `self._slot_dir = _default_lock_dir() / _sanitize_name(name)`).
- **Q2 (agent, resolved by inspection):** Do both lanes and every acquisition
  site flow through one function? **Answer:** Yes — `_cached_runner` (legacy
  callers), `paced_runner`'s `_paced` body and the fast-lane per-test rerun all
  use `_test_concurrency_slot`; `run_cached` calls the runner only on a miss, so
  cache hits never acquire a slot. Evidence:
  `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` (`_test_concurrency_slot`, `_cached_runner`,
  `paced_runner`, `_rerun_flaky`). Confirms A4 and AC4 without a second
  implementation.
- **Q3 (agent, resolved by inspection):** Which marker semantics do the ACs
  actually require — the guard's set-if-absent, or publish-own-value? **Answer:**
  Publish the pool actually held and restore the previous value (D1): AC1
  requires the value to identify the held pool *and* requires a nested hold to
  restore the outer value. The guard's shape is preserved (temporary, scoped,
  restored in `finally`). Evidence: AC1 wording; `run_tests.py::guarded_run_all`
  marker lifecycle.
- **Q4 (agent, resolved by inspection):** Which documents and fixtures carry
  the opt-in convention that AC6/AC7 must update? **Answer:**
  `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` §0.6 (and the §0.5 env table),
  `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (the finish-gate nested-run sentence),
  the `run_tests.py` module/`_test_concurrency_slot` docstrings,
  `process_semaphore.py` docstrings and `conftest.py` lines ~204–216. No
  doc-conformance test pins this wording (grepped `tests/` for §0.6 / marker
  phrases), so the docs can be rewritten without test churn. Call-site fixtures
  (`tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py`, `tests/test_pytest_path_resolution.py`,
  `tests/test_run_tests_cache.py`, `test_pre_push_gate_*`,
  `skill/test/tests/test_guarded_run_all.py`, `tests/test_validate_test_fanout.py`)
  keep working unchanged because explicit `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` still wins (AC3).
- **Q5 (agent, resolved by inspection):** Where does a derived directory live
  and how is it kept unique? **Answer:** `<marker-base>/nested/<pid>-<nonce>`
  (AC2's suggested shape; A3's per-invocation rule), under one `nested/` parent
  so a future prune can target it. The explicit helper keeps its existing
  `<base>/pi-semaphores` shape, so nothing that calls it today changes.
- **Q6 (agent, resolved by inspection):** Does this need child work items?
  **Answer:** No — D5 above: one atomic slice, and the neighbouring items in
  this family are leaves. Test-first ordering is preserved as steps 1–2.

**Producer review notes (non-blocking).** D1 (marker publish semantics) and D5
(single slice rather than a tests-then-implementation pair of children) are the
two judgement calls worth a reviewer's glance. Neither blocks implementation
and no question above needs an answer to proceed.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-14 — plan session (dispatched by `herdr-downtime`): pre-check
  `decision: plan` (Small / Medium), approval gate `request_approval: false`,
  duplicate-work check (no overlapping completed item; `SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86` is
  the predecessor, `SA-0MVB713IZ000NO42` a rebase-only overlap). Six review
  stages + AC-coverage review applied (AC4 gained an explicit marker-less
  contention test; AC7 sweep recorded). Added this plan + Appendix; no child
  work items created (D5); stage set to `plan_complete`; effort/risk
  refreshed.

data.description:
# Intake: Test cache — single-flight coalescing for identical in-flight suite runs

## Problem statement

The per-repo test cache (`skill/test_cache.py`) dedupes only **completed** runs at
the same git state (2 h TTL). Two agents that both miss the cache at the identical
command + git state therefore execute the full suite **concurrently**, each holding
a host-wide `"test"` slot and each doing the same 1.5–7 minute work. With nested-run
isolation (SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86) making the host-wide pool the only contention point,
the next structural reduction is single-flight: the second caller should wait on the
first in-flight run's result rather than acquiring its own slot and re-running.

## Users

- **Agents executing a suite through the test skill** — the `run_tests.py` CLI
  (via `paced_runner`), the audit F3 auto-run, and `implement.py`'s finish-gate
  suites (`_run_cached_paced`). This is the primary user.
- **The producer / standup** — indirectly: gate verdicts arrive sooner because two
  identical suites no longer compete for the same two host-wide slots.

User stories:

- *As an agent that just missed the test cache while another session is already
  running the identical suite, I want to receive that session's verdict instead of
  executing a duplicate, so that the host's scarce test slots are not wasted on the
  same work.*
- *As an agent waiting on a gate, I want a coalesced wait to be bounded and to fall
  back to a real run when the holder dies, so that coalescing can never turn a
  duplicate run into a hang.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — In-flight markers publish and always clear.** A cache-missing run
  publishes an in-flight marker keyed by (normalized command, git state, scope,
  test_type) **before** executing, and clears it on every exit path: success,
  non-zero exit, raised exception, timeout, and the mid-run checkout-movement
  quarantine path. No marker survives a completed `run_cached()` call.
- **AC2 — Coalescing.** A second caller finding a **fresh** marker for the
  identical key waits for that run's stored result (bounded by `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`)
  instead of executing a duplicate; it must not consume a test slot while waiting.
  When the marker is **stale** (holder process gone, or marker age beyond the
  documented bound) the caller reclaims it and executes normally; when the holder
  finishes without storing an entry (quarantined/unfingerprintable state) the waiter
  executes normally rather than returning an empty verdict. Any error creating,
  reading or waiting on a marker degrades to a plain execution — never a lost run and
  never a false verdict.
- **AC3 — No correctness change.** Cache hit/store/TTL/scope/test_type/provenance
  semantics are unchanged. A coalesced caller receives a result dict with the **same
  keys** as a cache miss + run, identical in value semantics, plus the additive
  marker `coalesced: true` (non-coalesced results gain `coalesced: false`), so no
  existing consumer changes behaviour.
- **AC4 — Bounded, no new deadlock.** A coalesced wait never exceeds
  `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, cannot deadlock (the waiter holds no slot while waiting, so it
  cannot block the holder; stale markers expire; a crashed holder is detectable by
  marker PID liveness and by marker age), and nested/cascaded runs
  (`LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` set) bypass coalescing so an outer run can never wait on
  a nested run it is itself blocking.
- **AC5 — Deterministic tests.** Tests in `tests/test_test_cache.py` cover:
  (a) two callers with the same key execute the command exactly once and the second
  gets `coalesced: true` with the first's verdict; (b) different keys (command, scope
  or test_type differing) still execute independently; (c) a stale marker
  (dead PID / aged marker) does not block and the caller executes; (d) cache hits,
  `force=True`, `no_cache=True` and nested runs bypass coalescing entirely (no marker
  is written, nothing waits); (e) the marker is cleared on the exception and timeout
  paths; (f) a holder that finishes without storing an entry leaves the waiter to
  execute rather than return an empty verdict; (g) a marker-create/read/wait error
  degrades to a normal execution; and (h) `test_cache`'s coalesce-bound default is
  pinned to `run_tests.TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT` (600 s) so the two cannot drift
  (the import-cycle guard). Tests must be deterministic — no wall-clock sleeps longer
  than a bounded poll, injected clock/runner where needed.
- **AC6 — Telemetry.** The coalesced wait is observable (e.g. additive
  `coalesced_wait_seconds` in the result, reported by the test skill's aggregate the
  way `slot_wait_seconds` is) so the contention-telemetry item
  (SA-0MVEDMM3N004Y6MO) can measure how often coalescing fires and how long it waits.
- **AC7 — Docs.** `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` §0 documents the coalescing
  contract: marker location, key composition, freshness bound, bypass conditions
  (cache hit, `--force`, `--no-cache`, nested run), the `coalesced` result field, the
  cross-host freshness rule (PID liveness is only meaningful for a marker whose
  `hostname` matches; otherwise the age bound decides) and the pre-run/post-run key
  nuance that makes a churned-tree miss safe.
- **AC8 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes**, including
  code comments/docstrings, `skill/test_cache.py` module docs, and the test-skill
  reference.
- **AC9 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes (build → test →
  commit order).

## Impact

Agents that would previously have burned both host-wide test slots re-running the
same suite now share one run's verdict, so gate checks come back sooner and
concurrent sessions stop duplicating minutes of identical work.

## Constraints

- **Must not weaken the two-slot host-wide ceiling.** This reduces duplicated work;
  it does not raise `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` (6) / `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_FAST` (4).
- **Per-repo and worktree-aware.** Markers live beside the cache entries
  (`cache_dir()`), honouring the existing git-state fingerprint; a marker must never
  coalesce runs from a different repository or a different tree.
- **No import cycle.** `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` imports `test_cache`, so
  `test_cache` must not import `run_tests`. The coalesce bound must therefore be read
  in `test_cache` from `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` with the same 600 s default, and a test
  must pin the two defaults together so they cannot drift.
- **Failure to coalesce is always safe.** Any error in marker creation, reading or
  waiting degrades to a normal execution — never to a lost run or a false verdict.
- Full project test suite must pass (build → test → commit order).

## Existing state

- `run_cached()` (`skill/test_cache.py`) is the single cache entry point for all
  three consumers. It computes the fingerprint, looks up, and on a miss calls
  `runner(normalized, cwd, timeout)` bracketed by
  `snapshot_own_checkout` / `compare_own_checkout_states`, then stores the entry.
- Cache entry layout: `<cache_dir>/<key>/{metadata.json, stdout.txt, stderr.txt}`;
  `key = sha256(normalized command + \0 + git state [+ \0type:<t>])[:32]`. **`scope`
  is metadata, not part of the cache key**, compared after lookup.
- `cache_dir()` resolves `<repo>/.worklog/cache/`, else `<git-dir>/test-cache/`,
  else `<repo>/.test-cache/` — per-repo and worktree-aware.
- "Writes are atomic (temp file + `os.replace`); no locking is used" — there is no
  in-flight/lock concept in the cache today.
- **Lookup keys on the pre-run state, the store keys on the post-run state.** A miss
  looks up under the fingerprint taken *before* the runner, but a completed run is
  stored under the fingerprint taken *afterwards* (so a finished run is always
  queryable — WL-0MVPO9P610055UQ3). A coalesced waiter therefore polls with **its
  own** pre-run fingerprint and never recomputes it mid-wait: when the tree churned
  during the holder's run the waiter's lookup misses, it executes normally, and no
  wrong verdict is ever served.
- `paced_runner()` (`run_tests.py`) wraps the runner so only **real executions**
  acquire a `"test"` slot; cache hits never take a slot. It calls `on_wait(queued_at,
  wait_seconds)` after acquisition. `Semaphore` is `flock`-based (kernel releases on
  death, so no stale slots), arrival-ordered, jittered, bounded by
  `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` (default 600 s) with lanes `full`/`fast`.
- `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` is the existing recursion marker for nested/cascaded runs.

## Desired change

1. **Marker store.** `<cache_dir>/inflight/<inflight_key>.json`, written with
   `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` (atomic create-wins → no lock needed). Key =
   `sha256(normalized command + git state + scope + test_type + fingerprint_kind)`.
   Payload: `pid`, `hostname`, `started_at` (epoch), `command`, `git_state`, `scope`,
   `test_type`, `fingerprint_kind`.
2. **Publish/clear.** In `run_cached()`, after a lookup miss and before the runner,
   attempt to create the marker inside a `try/finally` that removes it on every exit
   path (including the `STATE_CHANGED_EXIT_CODE` quarantine return and exceptions).
3. **Coalesce.** If creation fails because a fresh marker exists, poll (bounded by
   `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, jittered cadence, no slot held) for `lookup()` to succeed for
   the identical key/scope/kind; on success return that entry with `coalesced: true`.
   Freshness = holder PID alive (`os.kill(pid, 0)`) **and** marker age below a
   documented bound (queue wait `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` + command timeout + slack).
   Stale markers are reclaimed (unlinked) and the caller proceeds to execute. If the
   marker disappears with no stored entry, the caller executes.
4. **Bypass.** No marker is written (and no waiting happens) for a cache hit,
   `force=True`, `no_cache=True`, an unfingerprintable state, or a nested run
   (`LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` set).
5. **Result parity + telemetry.** Additive `coalesced: bool` and
   `coalesced_wait_seconds: float` keys on the result dict; thread them through
   `run_suite()` / `run_all()` / `guarded_run_all()` aggregates the way `cached` and
   `slot_wait_seconds` are threaded today.
6. **Docs + tests.** Document the contract in `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` §0
   and add the deterministic tests listed in AC5.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/test_cache.py` — in-flight marker helpers (create/read/clear/reclaim), the
  coalesce wait loop, `coalesced`/`coalesced_wait_seconds` result keys, bypass rules,
  module-doc section, `__all__` exports.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — aggregate `coalesced` / `coalesced_wait_seconds`
  through `run_suite()` / `run_all()` / `guarded_run_all()` (additive; `paced_runner`
  unchanged).
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — §0 coalescing contract subsection.
- `tests/test_test_cache.py` — deterministic single-flight tests (AC5) plus the
  `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` default-parity test (import-cycle guard).
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — likely no change (additive result keys
  only); verify the finish-gate suite aggregation tolerates the new keys.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — coalescing hides a genuine re-run.** Two callers with the same command at
  the same git state *should* have identical verdicts; the existing cache already
  assumes this for completed runs, so coalescing adds no new assumption. Mitigation:
  the key is the same key the cache uses (plus scope/kind), so coalescing can never
  merge two states the cache would keep apart.
- **Risk — a slow starvation loop.** A waiter that repeatedly loses the marker race
  could re-queue. Mitigation: the wait is attempted at most once per `run_cached()`
  call, bounded by `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`; on timeout it executes normally.
- **Risk — queue-window staleness.** Markers are published **before** the pacer
  acquires a slot, so a holder may legitimately sit queued for up to
  `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`. Mitigation: freshness uses PID liveness as the primary signal
  with an age bound of `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT + command timeout + slack`, documented in
  the reference.
- **Risk — cross-host shared filesystem.** A marker written on one host carries a
  `hostname`; a waiter on another host cannot test PID liveness and must fall back to
  the age bound only. Documented; single-host operation is the supported case.
- **Risk — scope-creep.** Adjacent opportunities (e.g. coalescing *across* repos,
  coalescing audit semaphore waits, cache-keying scope) are explicitly out of scope;
  record them as linked work items rather than widening this item.
- **Assumption** — the additive `coalesced` key is acceptable to every consumer; each
  consumer is checked to read only the keys it needs.
- **Assumption** — `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` is a reliable "nested run" signal (it is
  the existing recursion marker for guard ownership); reusing it avoids inventing a
  second nesting concept.

## Related work

- **SA-0MVEDOF7A004TSWD** (completed) — staggered back-off under contention. This
  item's parent discovery: stave off the herd, then coalesce its redundant members.
- **SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86** (completed) — nested-run isolation; makes the top-level
  pool the only contention point, which is the precondition for this item.
- **SA-0MUA8BSAG000YZA2** (completed) — pacing telemetry (`on_wait`); the coalesced
  wait reuses its reporting shape (`*_wait_seconds`) rather than inventing a second
  measurement vocabulary.
- **SA-0MVEDMM3N004Y6MO** (in progress, intake_complete) — contention telemetry;
  consumes the `coalesced` / `coalesced_wait_seconds` signal produced here.
- **SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI** (completed) — arrival-ordered turnstile in the semaphore;
  complementary fairness work, unchanged by coalescing.
- **SA-0MVEJIRZ60017H4V** (open, idea) — unify the test-cache namespace across
  worktrees and the main checkout. Markers live under `cache_dir()`, so that item
  would also unify the marker namespace. No dependency edge either way: coalescing is
  correct under both the current per-checkout namespace and a unified one.
- `skill/test_cache.py` — the cache being extended; `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py`
  — the slot pool whose `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` bounds the wait.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview round was required: the seed context (discovery notes from
SA-0MVEDOF7A004TSWD plus the six seed acceptance criteria) was sufficient to draft the
brief without asking questions answerable by repo inspection. Design decisions taken
by the agent, recorded for audit rather than presented as questions:

- Q: Should coalescing live in `run_cached` or in the pacer (`paced_runner`)?
  — **Decision (agent, from repo evidence):** `run_cached`, because that is the single
  entry point for all three consumers, and because publishing *before* slot acquisition
  also collapses duplicates that are merely **queued** (the dominant case under a
  herd). Source: `skill/test_cache.py::run_cached`,
  `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py::paced_runner`,
  `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py::_run_cached_paced`.
- Q: Where does the coalesce bound come from, given `test_cache` cannot import
  `run_tests` (import cycle)? — **Decision (agent):** read `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` in
  `test_cache` with the same 600 s default, and pin the two defaults together with a
  test. Source: `run_tests.py:153` (`from test_cache import ...`) proves the cycle.
- Q: How is staleness detected without PID bookkeeping? — **Decision (agent):** PID
  liveness (`os.kill(pid, 0)`) plus `hostname` plus a documented age bound; the marker
  is a plain file, reclaimed by the waiter, so no lock server and no stale-lock class
  of bug is introduced. Source: `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` (flock/creat-based
  precedent, "no PID bookkeeping" for *locks* — markers differ and record a PID
  deliberately, because a dead holder must be detectable before the age bound).
- **OPEN QUESTION (deferred, non-blocking):** none.

## Appendix: Plan review (code inspection)

No plan interview was required either: every plan-level question was answerable by
repo inspection, so the six review stages ran against the existing brief and applied
only intent-preserving clarifications. Decisions recorded for audit:

- Q: Can a coalesced waiter poll `lookup()` under the key the holder will *store*
  under? — **Decision (agent):** it need not, and must not assume so. `run_cached`
  looks up under the pre-run fingerprint but stores under the post-run one, so the
  waiter polls with its own pre-run fingerprint (never recomputing it mid-wait). When
  the tree churned during the holder's run the waiter misses, executes normally, and
  no wrong verdict is served. Source: `skill/test_cache.py::run_cached`.
- Q: Would any consumer break on the additive `coalesced*` keys? — **Decision
  (agent):** no. `implement.py` renders gate facts from the explicit allow-list
  `GATE_FACT_FIELDS`, documented as additive ("a consumer reading an older result
  simply finds no key"), so an unknown key is simply not surfaced. Surfacing
  `coalesced_wait_seconds` in the gate report belongs to the contention-telemetry
  item (SA-0MVEDMM3N004Y6MO), not here. Source:
  `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py::GATE_FACT_FIELDS`.
- Q: Should the change be decomposed into child features? — **Decision (agent):** no.
  It is one vertical slice through `test_cache` → `run_tests` aggregation → docs →
  tests. Splitting the tests from the implementation would leave a test-first child
  red at its own finish gate, so one item keeps build → test → commit coherent; the
  family's precursors (SA-0MVEDOF7A004TSWD, SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86,
  SA-0MUA8BSAG000YZA2) were single items with no children for the same reason.
- Q: Is AC7's "§0" target accurate? — **Decision (agent):** yes.
  `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` §0 "Cached execution (default)" is the cache
  contract section (with sub-sections 0.1–0.6 in place), so coalescing lands as a new
  §0.x there.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-14 — plan review applied (no AC added, removed or weakened): AC2 now states
  the failure-to-coalesce-degrades-to-execution rule; AC5 gained the marker-error and
  `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` default-parity tests (both already required by the Constraints);
  AC7 gained the cross-host and churned-tree documentation requirements; *Existing
  state* records the pre-run lookup / post-run store key asymmetry; Related work links
  SA-0MVEJIRZ60017H4V; Appendix records the four review decisions. Decomposition
  decision: single item, no children.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MVEDOF7A004TSWD** – Test semaphore: staggered back-off under contention to prevent thundering-herd waits (completed)
- **SA-0MWATUPEW007OBIU** – Residual post-fix slot waits still breach parent thresholds (re-measurement follow-up) (completed)
- **SA-0MSGNUXT3009LV7S** – Implement: wire cache into run_tests.py (completed)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+467 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: 0mua8bsag000yza2, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+459 more)
